meta.title: 🔴 Drinks with Raoul Pal: Ask Me Anything
meta.thread_line: 5 threads · macro spring into the banana zone · inflation falls, the ISM turns · buy, hold, add until 2030 · Solana, Coinbase, Tesla and MicroStrategy calls · gold, energy and the UK investor problem

snapshot: A November 2023 Friday drinks AMA from Grand Cayman; Raoul Pal answers Real Vision members' questions over a Gramona cava.
His frame: 2022 priced the recession; 2023 is macro and crypto spring, moving into a year-end **banana zone**, then summer in 2024 and a 'batshit crazy' 2025.
Year to date by his count: Nasdaq almost +50%, exponential-age tech basket +63%, Bitcoin +119%, Ethereum +63%, Solana **+500%**.
Inflation is mean-reverting: back to 2% or lower, likely negative including core in this cycle; zero chance of a December Fed hike.
He hasn't sold a single crypto holding since buying aggressively in **April 2020** and plans to run most of it to 2030.
Calls: Coinbase over Tesla for two months, Solana over Ethereum for six; MicroStrategy likely trades at a discount once a spot Bitcoin ETF exists.
Corrections in an election year: maybe two of about 10%, at most 15%; buy them.

themes.title: Macro spring into the banana zone, then summer in 2024 and a wild 2025
themes.lead: Pal says macro and crypto run on the same liquidity cycle, which since 2008 lines up election years with Bitcoin halvings.
bullets: 2022 was the bear market: growth tech down about 70%, crypto 70-80%, Nasdaq priced an ISM of **38** that only reached 46.
He bought Ethereum first in June 2022, then crypto and tech in Oct-Dec 2022, and has added since.
Late spring brings the **banana zone**: a fast year-end rally that underweight institutions chase.
Macro summer (2024) = falling rates and inflation, rising unemployment, growth turning up from the floor; same timing as the election year and halving.
2025 is usually the exponential year before winter, when rates rise and markets pull back.
Election-year corrections: maybe two of about 10%, max **15%**.
He credits his 'everything code' thesis, first written in Global Macro Investor, for being 'spookily right' so far.

quote.text: macro spring and crypto spring are the same thing because macro is crypto

themes.watch: He frames this probabilistically, 'no guarantees'; he founded and promotes Real Vision, which sells the research he cites.

themes.title: Inflation falls through 2024, the ISM turns, and liquidity rises
themes.lead: Invest 6-18 months ahead: the recession is priced, and forward indicators point to growth picking up.
bullets: Recession this quarter and next is likely but irrelevant unless you trade the Russell 2000, oil or copper.
Inflation goes to **2% or lower**, likely negative, core too; he thinks the Fed wants lower rates to refinance debt.
Rates come significantly lower (1-2%); zero is unknown and doesn't matter.
ISM new orders minus inventories says the ISM is above **50** within three to four months; no double dip, which he says has never happened since 1990 except 2001.
Fed net liquidity is up **10%** this year; GMI liquidity year on year is positive; China is looking to stimulate, so 2024 is 'the year of stimulus'.
Debasement marks assets up rather than buying them (as in Argentina, Venezuela, Iran, Turkey): when 20 billionaires show up, every house gaps higher.
Lagging assets: NFTs bottomed about **15 months** after the Ethereum economy; Rolex and Patek Philippe prices still fall, with recovery in 2024-25.

quote.text: don't invest in today it's the biggest mistake everybody makes in markets

themes.title: Buy, hold, add into dips, and run it to 2030
themes.lead: His own Bitcoin history taught him that selling early cost far more than any drawdown.
bullets: Bought Bitcoin in 2013 at **$200** as a 10-year bet; valued it at $1 million, discounted 90% to $100,000.
It rose 5x, fell 85%, ran 10x into 2017; he sold at $2,000-2,500 and watched it reach $20,000.
Re-entered April 2020 near $6,500 and bought up to about $12,000; holding the original stake would have made 5x more, adding within 30% of lows 25x more.
Plan: take a little off the table, run most of it until **2030**; no stablecoins, full crypto exposure.
Rules: buy and hold, no leverage, cold storage (exchange, then Ledger), no FOMO; he still holds a small Solana bag bought at $189.
He avoids staking yield: native staking tokens are like emerging-market local bonds, the yield gets paid while the currency can go to zero, as with Luna.
Crypto is the best-performing asset three years of every four; Druckenmiller, Paul Tudor Jones, Soros, Louis Bacon and Steve Cohen trade it, he says.

quote.text: since I started buying aggressively in April 2020 I've not sold a single thing

themes.watch: He is an investor in smaller tokens and venture deals, so 'everything looks amazing' comes with exposure.

names.name: Ethereum (ETH)
names.blurb: Core bet with Solana; ETF could end its lag.

themes.title: Solana over Ethereum, Coinbase over Tesla, and avoid MicroStrategy
themes.lead: Asked to choose, he favors the higher-beta asset in each pair.
bullets: Six months: **Solana** over Ethereum; the Solana trade since his GMI note two months ago 'shocked me'; liquidity pushes Solana up more than Bitcoin.
Two months: **Coinbase**, though very bullish Tesla; Coinbase probably makes a new all-time high by 2025 and goes up more than Tesla.
Tesla is held back by high rates hitting car buyers and explodes when rates fall; he calls it the most important company in the world, with **$29 billion** of cash.
**MicroStrategy** likely trades at a discount to its Bitcoin, as GBTC did, once a spot ETF tracks Bitcoin one for one; steer clear.
Smaller bags (XRP, Doge, Avalanche, Matic) are leftover shrapnel; Chainlink and The Graph 'look great', but alt season is only starting.
To a viewer chasing Avalanche: that is FOMO; ask if Ethereum rises over two years.

quote.text: I think coinbase probably goes up more and they're both really high quality companies

themes.title: Gold, energy, uranium and the UK investor problem
themes.lead: Outside crypto and tech he likes gold and uranium, but expects everything to underperform tech, and tech to underperform crypto.
bullets: **Gold** should break $2,000; without tech and crypto he'd call it one of the best 12-month risk-reward bets.
Energy stocks rise in macro summer but underperform tech over 20-30 years.
Uranium and copper share the cheap-energy thesis; he worries the Sprott-driven retail crowd 'gets rinsed'.
Carbon allowances lag the ISM; his trade has done nothing and should work once ISM is back above 50.
UK and European markets have gone nowhere for 20 years, so UK investors take currency risk in US tech; the dollar is in a secular bear market; Europeans 'just buy LVMH'.

names.name: LVMH
names.blurb: The one European winner, he jokes.

takeaways.title: Position 6-18 months ahead using forward liquidity and ISM new orders, not today's data
Buy corrections of 10-15% in election years rather than trading around them
Hold in cold storage without leverage; skip staking yield that adds counterparty risk
Prefer a spot Bitcoin ETF over MicroStrategy for pure exposure

claims.claim: Inflation falls to 2% or lower and likely goes negative, including core, this cycle.
The ISM goes above 50 within three to four months.
Zero chance the Fed raises rates in December.
Election-year corrections are at most about 15%.
Coinbase most likely hits a new all-time high by 2025.
MicroStrategy will trade at a discount to its Bitcoin holdings and underperform once a spot ETF exists.

claims.claim: 2024 is a strong year and 2025 even better before the cycle turns.

Recommendations: Gramona Imperial cava, home-roasted pumpkin seeds with black salt, a gin martini over vodka, Estrella from Barcelona in a small cold caña, 1996 Dom Perignon, the band Jungle ('Heavy, California'); Cayman builders Phoenix Construction and Edgewater Development.

Sources referenced: Stan Druckenmiller (invest on forward information), Jordi Visser's end-of-business-cycle thesis, his own Global Macro Investor (19-year track record) and Real Vision Pro Macro, an upcoming exponential-age list portfolio built with Julian Bittel.
